explanation: Bronchodilators relax tightened airway muscles, making them the primary treatment for sudden breathing constriction or asthma attacks. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h4)

question: A patient with thick, sticky mucus blocking their airways is most likely to be prescribed which type of inhalable medication?

options.A: Beta-blockers
options.B: Anticoagulants
options.C: Vasopressors
options.D: Mucolytics

explanation: Mucolytics are specifically designed to break down and thin thick respiratory secretions so they can be cleared more easily. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h4)

question: What is the best body position for a patient receiving inhalation therapy?

options.A: Flat on the back with a low pillow
options.B: Lying flat on the left side
options.C: Pronated face down on the bed
options.D: Upright sitting or high Fowler's position

explanation: Sitting upright allows the diaphragm to move freely and promotes maximum lung expansion during medication delivery. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h5)

question: Why must a nurse assess a patient's breathing technique and coordination before handing them an inhaler?

options.A: Assessment ensures the patient will never experience any drug side effects
options.B: All inhalation devices function identically regardless of the patient's skill
options.C: Patients are legally required to pass a written test before treatment
options.D: Different devices require specific breathing maneuvers for the drug to work

explanation: An MDI requires slow, deep breaths with a spacer, while a DPI requires a sharp inhalation, so matching technique is critical. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h5)

question: How long should a patient typically hold their breath after inhaling a dose of medication from an inhaler?

options.A: Until they feel dizzy
options.B: No more than one second
options.C: Exactly one minute
options.D: About 10 seconds

explanation: Holding the breath for about 10 seconds allows the tiny medication particles time to settle deep into the lung tissue instead of being exhaled right away. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h6)

question: What should the nurse instruct the patient to do immediately before actuating a metered-dose inhaler?

options.A: Inhale as fast as possible through the nose
options.B: Hyperventilate for thirty seconds
options.C: Exhale completely to empty the lungs
options.D: Take a quick swallow of cold water

explanation: Exhaling fully clears space in the lungs so the subsequent slow, deep inhalation can pull maximum medication into the airways. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h6)

question: Which complication can occur if a patient fails to rinse their mouth after using an inhaled corticosteroid?

options.A: Sudden closure of the vocal cords
options.B: Severe inflammation of the esophagus
options.C: Oral fungal infection or thrush
options.D: Permanent discoloration of the teeth

explanation: Residual steroid powder left in the oral cavity alters normal flora, frequently causing fungal overgrowth known as oral thrush. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h7)

question: Why might a patient experience a fast heartbeat (tachycardia) and hand tremors after using a rescue inhaler?

options.A: The inhaler device was shaken upside down before use
options.B: The patient drank cold water right before taking the medication
options.C: The medication has a systemic stimulant effect on beta receptors
options.D: The patient held their breath for too long during administration

explanation: Rescue inhalers often contain beta-agonists which, when absorbed into the bloodstream, stimulate the heart and nervous system. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h7)

question: When a patient is prescribed both a bronchodilator and an inhaled corticosteroid, which one should they generally use first?

options.A: Whichever medication is closer to hand
options.B: The corticosteroid to coat the throat
options.C: The bronchodilator to open the airways
options.D: Neither, they must be mixed together first

explanation: Using the bronchodilator first opens up the air passages, allowing the subsequent corticosteroid to penetrate much deeper into the lungs. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h8)

question: A home care nurse is reviewing proper maintenance with a client who uses a metered-dose inhaler. What instruction should the nurse include?

options.A: Never clean the plastic mouthpiece housing to preserve the internal valve
options.B: Store the active inhaler device inside a humid bathroom cabinet
options.C: Check the built-in dose counter regularly to avoid running out of medication
options.D: Wash the pressurized metal canister inside a dishwasher once every week

explanation: Monitoring the dose counter ensures patients know when their medication is running low or empty before an emergency arises. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h8)

question: What main substance does a Nelson inhaler deliver to help a patient breathe better?

options.A: Dry chemical powder
options.B: Medicated steam
options.C: Oxygen gas
options.D: Sterile saline mist

explanation: Spot on! The Nelson inhaler is a classic bedside tool used to vaporize hot water and soothing drugs so the patient breathes in warm, comforting medicated steam.

question: Why is moist heat therapy so helpful for a patient dealing with chest and airway congestion?

options.A: It expands the lung tissue to increase total capacity
options.B: It loosens thick mucus and soothes irritated airways
options.C: It kills all bacterial infections in the chest instantly
options.D: It cools down body temperature during a high fever

explanation: You got it! Warm moisture works like magic to thin out sticky, thick mucus in the upper airway, making it much easier to cough up while calming down raw, irritated throat linings.

question: What is the job of the air inlet on a Nelson inhaler?

options.A: It locks the cork lid tightly into the ceramic jar
options.B: It lets the nurse pour medicine in while treating
options.C: It acts as a drain for extra water collection
options.D: It allows fresh air to mix with the rising steam

explanation: Exactly! The air inlet lets a bit of cooler room air mix with the vapor. This keeps the steam from being too scorching hot for the patient's mouth and throat.

question: What purpose does the cork bung serve when using a Nelson inhaler?

options.A: It filters out dust particles before the patient breathes the vapor
options.B: It seals the top of the jar so steam escapes only through the mouthpiece
options.C: It measures the exact temperature of the water inside the container
options.D: It absorbs excess medication that spills during preparation

explanation: Well done! The cork acts as a tight lid, making sure all the warm steam is forced to travel upward through the central tube and out the mouthpiece where the patient needs it.

question: Which of these conditions is a classic reason to use a Nelson inhaler?

options.A: Acute sinusitis
options.B: Bacterial pneumonia
options.C: Spontaneous pneumothorax
options.D: Pulmonary edema

explanation: Spot on! Sinusitis brings painful inflammation and blocked nasal passages, which respond wonderfully to the warm, soothing moisture of steam therapy.

question: A patient has severe laryngitis with a painful, raspy voice and is given steam inhalation. What is the main goal here?

options.A: To deliver systemic antibiotics directly into the bloodstream
options.B: To force deep lung expansion in the lower alveoli
options.C: To soothe inflamed vocal cords and mucosal tissues
options.D: To permanently cure the viral infection overnight

explanation: You got it! Moist heat hydrates dry, raw throat tissues, taking away that scratchy irritation and giving sore vocal cords a chance to rest and heal.

question: Which common substance is often added to hot water in a Nelson inhaler to ease breathing?

options.A: Liquid paraffin wax
options.B: Intravenous saline
options.C: Tincture of benzoin
options.D: Hydrogen peroxide

explanation: Correct! Tincture of benzoin (or menthol) is a classic bedside additive that adds comforting, aromatic vapors to the steam.

question: Why must you carefully check the ceramic jar for cracks before pouring in boiling water?

options.A: To measure the exact volume capacity in milliliters
options.B: To remove leftover food particles from previous treatments
options.C: To ensure the inside is completely sterile for surgical use
options.D: To check for cracks that could leak or shatter from thermal shock

explanation: Safety first! Pouring boiling water into a damaged ceramic jar can cause it to shatter completely from thermal shock, risking severe burns.

question: How should a patient breathe while using the mouthpiece of a Nelson inhaler?

options.A: Only through the nose with the mouth tightly closed
options.B: In through the mouth and out through the nose
options.C: In through the nose and out through the mouth
options.D: Using rapid, shallow panting breaths only

explanation: Spot on! Inhaling through the mouth draws the medicated vapor straight into the airways, while breathing out through the nose stops them from blowing vapor back into the device.

question: Up to what level should the nurse fill the Nelson inhaler jar with boiling water?

options.A: All the way to the very top rim
options.B: About two-thirds full
options.C: Only one-tenth full
options.D: Exactly five liters

explanation: You got it! Filling it about two-thirds full leaves plenty of room for steam to build up without the hot water bubbling over into the mouthpiece.

question: What is the biggest safety risk you must watch out for when using a Nelson inhaler?

options.A: Acute kidney failure
options.B: Scalding from hot water or steam
options.C: Sudden systemic drug toxicity
options.D: Permanent hearing loss

explanation: Spot on! Because you are working with boiling water, the main danger is accidental spills causing painful burns to the patient's skin or face.

question: An elderly patient starts feeling dizzy and lightheaded during steam therapy. What is your very first nursing action?

options.A: Stop the treatment and remove the inhaler immediately
options.B: Add more boiling water to increase vapor strength
options.C: Leave the room briefly to fetch a doctor
options.D: Encourage the patient to breathe faster and deeper

explanation: Safety comes first! If a patient feels dizzy or faint, halt the procedure right away to keep them safe from injury.

question: What should you do right after a patient finishes their steam inhalation session?

options.A: Spray the patient's throat with strong antiseptics
options.B: Assist the patient in wiping their mouth and face
options.C: Immediately place the boiling jar into an ice bath
options.D: Seal the dirty water inside the jar for laboratory testing

explanation: Exactly! Gently wiping their face clears away any condensed moisture or medicine residue so it doesn't dry on their skin and cause irritation.

question: Why should you wait for a Nelson inhaler to cool down before trying to wash it?

options.A: To ensure the plastic cork expands to its maximum size
options.B: To save electricity in the utility room
options.C: To let the medication completely dry into a hard solid crust
options.D: To prevent hand burns and avoid cracking the ceramic from sudden temperature changes

explanation: Spot on! Letting it cool protects your hands from burns and stops cold tap water from cracking the hot ceramic jar due to sudden thermal shock.

question: What is the primary physical form of medication delivered by a nebulizer to the patient's lungs?

options.A: A compressed gas tablet
options.B: A fine mist or aerosolized vapor
options.C: A warm liquid solution
options.D: A dry powder capsule

explanation: A nebulizer turns liquid medicine into a vapor so the patient can easily breathe it deep into the lungs. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h1)

question: Why is nebulization often chosen over other inhalers for patients in acute respiratory distress?

options.A: It requires only normal, quiet breathing instead of a deep, forced inhalation.
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for any vital sign monitoring.
options.C: It stops all lung infections within minutes of starting the treatment.
options.D: It works ten times faster than any intravenous medication available.

explanation: Patients struggling to catch their breath cannot coordinate deep inhalers, making normal breathing through a nebulizer mask much easier. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h1)

question: Which medication group is most commonly given via nebulizer to relax tightened airway muscles?

options.A: Vasopressors
options.B: Anticoagulants
options.C: Antibiotics
options.D: Bronchodilators

explanation: Bronchodilators open up constricted breathing tubes so air can flow freely in and out of the lungs. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h2)

question: A patient arrives at the clinic with thick, sticky mucus blocking their airways and causing severe coughing. Which type of nebulized medication is most appropriate?

options.A: A local anesthetic
options.B: A beta-blocker
options.C: A mucolytic agent
options.D: An intravenous fluid

explanation: Mucolytics specifically target and break down thick pulmonary secretions, making them easier for the patient to expel. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h2)

question: What is the main reason for assessing lung sounds before giving a nebulizer treatment?

options.A: To clear out thick mucus plugs before the machine is turned on
options.B: To establish a baseline for evaluating the treatment's effectiveness later
options.C: To find out if the patient has a hidden bacterial chest infection
options.D: To calculate the exact dose of medicine needed for the patient

explanation: Checking lung sounds beforehand helps the nurse compare wheezing or air entry after the treatment ends. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h3)

question: Which physical sign indicates that a patient is experiencing severe respiratory distress before treatment?

options.A: A quiet, relaxed breathing pattern while lying flat
options.B: Pink skin color on the cheeks and nail beds
options.C: Use of accessory neck and chest muscles to breathe
options.D: A slow, even heart rate of 60 beats per minute

explanation: Straining neck and chest muscles means the body is working extra hard to pull air into struggling lungs. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h3)

question: What is the usual gas flow rate range set on the flowmeter for a standard compressor nebulizer?

options.A: 20 to 25 liters per minute
options.B: 12 to 15 liters per minute
options.C: 6 to 8 liters per minute
options.D: 1 to 2 liters per minute

explanation: A flow rate of 6 to 8 liters per minute provides enough pressure to turn the liquid medicine into a proper mist. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h4)

question: Why is sterile normal saline sometimes added to the medication cup during preparation?

options.A: To reach the proper total liquid volume needed for the nebulizer cup to aerosolize correctly
options.B: To permanently neutralize any harmful side effects caused by bronchodilators
options.C: To numb the lining of the throat so the patient does not cough
options.D: To clean the plastic tubing before the medication mist passes through it

explanation: Nebulizer cups need a minimum fluid volume, often 3 to 5 mL, to create an effective aerosol mist. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h4)

question: What position should the nurse place the patient in before starting a nebulizer treatment?

options.A: Flat on their back with no pillows
options.B: Toned flat on their stomach
options.C: Lying strictly on their left side
options.D: Upright sitting or semi-Fowler's position

explanation: Sitting upright lets the chest expand fully, helping the medication travel deep into the lower airways. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h5)

question: Why does the nurse occasionally tap the side of the medication cup during the procedure?

options.A: To prevent the plastic parts from overheating while the compressor runs
options.B: To help remaining liquid droplets slide down into the bottom of the cup to be aerosolized
options.C: To signal to the patient that the treatment session is halfway finished
options.D: To clear any dust blocking the outside air filter vents

explanation: Tapping the cup drops clinging fluid back into the reservoir so it doesn't go to waste on the walls. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h5)

question: What is the best immediate action for the nurse to take after the nebulizer cup runs dry?

options.A: Reassess lung sounds and measure the patient's oxygen saturation
options.B: Immediately start a second dose of medication without waiting
options.C: Disconnect the air flow meter and leave the room quietly
options.D: Instruct the patient to lie flat in bed for one hour

explanation: Checking lung sounds and oxygen levels right after treatment confirms whether the bronchodilator opened the airways successfully. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h6)

question: After a bronchodilator nebulizer treatment, a patient coughs heavily. What should the nurse encourage them to do next?

options.A: Swallow the mucus to keep the throat moist
options.B: Expectorate the loosened mucus into a tissue
options.C: Drink a large glass of ice-cold water immediately
options.D: Lie down flat on the bed to stop coughing

explanation: Coughing brings up the loosened secretions, so spitting them out into a tissue clears the airway safely. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h6)

question: Which common side effect often occurs due to the stimulant properties of bronchodilators like albuterol?

options.A: Rapid heart rate and palpitations
options.B: Uncontrollable drowsiness and sleep
options.C: Severe drop in blood pressure
options.D: Complete loss of the sense of taste

explanation: Beta-agonist bronchodilators stimulate heart receptors, frequently causing a fast heartbeat or jittery feeling. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h7)

question: What should the nurse do FIRST if a patient suddenly develops severe wheezing and increased breathing distress right after starting a nebulizer?

options.A: Wait ten minutes to see if the reaction goes away on its own
options.B: Stop the nebulizer treatment immediately and assess the patient
options.C: Ask the patient to lie flat and take deep, fast breaths
options.D: Turn up the air flow meter to make the mist spray faster

explanation: Worsening distress means a possible paradoxical bronchospasm, so stopping the drug is the immediate safety priority. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h7)

question: Why is proper cleaning and drying of nebulizer equipment so critical for patient safety?

options.A: Dirty equipment will permanently break the air compressor motor
options.B: Washing prevents the plastic mask from changing color over time
options.C: Moist plastic parts easily grow harmful bacteria that can cause lung infections
options.D: Leftover medication residue turns into a solid metal inside the tube

explanation: Wet nebulizer cups are breeding grounds for germs, which the patient would inhale directly into their lungs during the next treatment. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h8)

question: What is the correct way to dry nebulizer parts after washing them?

options.A: Air dry them completely on a clean paper towel or lint-free cloth
options.B: Blow hot air through them using a standard hair dryer on high heat
options.C: Place them inside a sealed plastic bag while they are still soaking wet
options.D: Wipe them dry using a heavily used cloth towel from the laundry bin

explanation: Air drying on a clean surface prevents germ transfer from dirty towels and ensures no moisture is trapped inside. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h8)

question: What is the main goal of using a steam tent for a patient?

options.A: To provide a cool environment for high fevers
options.B: To administer aerosolized systemic antibiotics
options.C: To increase total body fluid volume rapidly
options.D: To deliver warm, moist air to the respiratory tract

explanation: Great job! A steam tent traps moisture so the patient breathes in warm, humid air, which helps soothe and open up the airways.

question: How does the high humidity inside a steam tent help a patient with a heavy cough?

options.A: It dilates the tiny air sacs in the lower lungs
options.B: It kills bacterial infections in the upper airway
options.C: It numbs the throat nerves to stop the cough reflex
options.D: It liquefies thick mucus so it is easier to clear

explanation: Spot on! Moisture acts like magic on sticky mucus, thinning it out so the patient can cough it up easily.

question: Which breathing condition is most commonly treated with a steam tent?

options.A: Pulmonary embolism
options.B: Croup
options.C: Pneumothorax
options.D: Pleural effusion

explanation: You got it! Croup causes that classic barking cough, and warm, moist air is one of the best ways to bring relief.

question: A toddler comes in with a barking cough and noisy breathing (stridor). What should you, as the nurse, prepare for?

options.A: Prepare equipment for a steam tent
options.B: Administer a dry oxygen mask at high flow
options.C: Apply a cold ice pack to the chest wall
options.D: Insert a large-bore intravenous line immediately

explanation: That barking cough and stridor point straight to croup! Setting up humidified steam therapy is a key nursing action here.

question: Where should you position the steam generator in relation to the patient's bed?

options.A: Underneath the mattress for hidden warmth
options.B: Tied securely to the side rail of the crib
options.C: At a safe distance to prevent accidental burns
options.D: Directly inside the tent canopy next to the pillow

explanation: Safety first! Always keep the hot generator far enough away to protect the patient from burns.

question: Why is it important to check the electrical cord of the steam generator before turning it on?

options.A: To verify the correct voltage for the hospital room
options.B: To measure how much electricity the unit will use
options.C: To ensure the heating water boils much faster
options.D: To prevent electrical shocks and fire hazards

explanation: Spot on! Water and electricity are a dangerous mix, so checking cords keeps both you and your patient safe.

question: What is an important assessment to do BEFORE starting steam therapy?

options.A: Baseline respiratory rate and breath sounds
options.B: Baseline abdominal girth measurement
options.C: Fasting blood glucose level check
options.D: Complete neurological reflex testing

explanation: You need to know how they sound *before* treatment so you can tell if the steam is actually helping!

question: Why should a patient wear lightweight cotton clothing inside a steam tent instead of heavy synthetics?

options.A: Heavy clothes block the steam from reaching the lungs
options.B: Cotton fabrics absorb all the humidity completely
options.C: Cotton breathes better and prevents overheating
options.D: Synthetic fabrics melt easily when exposed to steam

explanation: Exactly! Cotton keeps the patient comfortable and stops them from getting too hot in a humid space.

question: How often should you check the patient's breathing during the early phase of steam therapy?

options.A: Every four hours
options.B: Only when the patient rings the bell
options.C: Every fifteen minutes
options.D: Once every shift

explanation: Checking frequently at the start ensures the patient is taking in the moisture well and their breathing is improving.

question: Why do you need to keep a close eye on the water level in the steam generator while it's running?

options.A: To prevent the reservoir from boiling completely dry
options.B: To prevent the plastic tent canopy from melting
options.C: To check if the patient is drinking enough water
options.D: To make sure the steam turns into cold mist

explanation: You got it! Letting the water run dry can ruin the machine and create a safety hazard.

question: What is the biggest safety hazard to watch out for during steam tent therapy?

options.A: Hypertensive crisis
options.B: Sudden hypoglycemia
options.C: Scald burns
options.D: Severe hypothermia

explanation: Correct! Because boiling water and hot steam are involved, burn prevention is always a top priority.

question: You need to add more water to a running steam generator. What is your very first step?

options.A: Ask the parent to hold the steam nozzle away
options.B: Pour cold water slowly while the unit is still boiling
options.C: Turn off and unplug the unit before adding water
options.D: Cover the hot metal parts with a dry towel first

explanation: Always power down and unplug first! This protects you from electrical shocks and nasty steam burns.

question: What is the safest way to open the steam tent when the treatment is done?

options.A: Rip open the plastic tent quickly to let fresh air rush in
options.B: Leave the steam running while taking the patient out
options.C: Turn off the generator and open the canopy gradually
options.D: Wait until the room temperature drops below normal

explanation: Opening it slowly prevents a sudden blast of cool air from chilling your damp patient.

question: Why should you do a quick physical assessment right after the steam session ends?

options.A: To check if the bed linens need washing
options.B: To evaluate how well the treatment worked
options.C: To see if the patient needs a snack or drink
options.D: To make sure the electrical cord is cool

explanation: Spot on! Comparing your notes now with your baseline check tells you if the therapy did its job.

question: Which of these details must you include when charting steam tent therapy?

options.A: The brand name of the plastic tent canopy
options.B: The exact electrical voltage of the wall socket
options.C: The name of the manufacturer who built the bed
options.D: Start and end times of the treatment

explanation: You got it! Accurate start and end times give a clear timeline of the care you provided.

question: Why is it important to write down how the patient tolerated the treatment and how much mucus they cleared?

options.A: It shows how much water the machine used up
options.B: It proves the effectiveness of the treatment
options.C: It determines the hospital room billing costs
options.D: It replaces the need for a physical assessment

explanation: Brilliant! Documenting their response helps the whole healthcare team see that the therapy was successful.

question: Which common, lightweight device uses two small prongs to deliver low-flow oxygen right into a patient's nostrils?

options.A: Non-rebreather mask
options.B: Venturi mask
options.C: Nasal cannula
options.D: Simple face mask

explanation: You'll see nasal cannulas everywhere in the ward! They're the standard, comfortable choice for giving patients a little extra oxygen through their nose.

question: As a nurse, why would you start a patient on nasal oxygen therapy?

options.A: To treat tissue hypoxia and raise low blood oxygen levels
options.B: To deliver high-pressure aerosolized medications to the lungs
options.C: To completely replace normal breathing mechanics during sleep
options.D: To prevent the patient from experiencing dry mouth overnight

explanation: Spot on! We give oxygen when the body's tissues aren't getting enough of it (hypoxia), helping to bring those blood oxygen levels back up to a safe place.

question: What equipment do you attach directly to an oxygen source to control how fast the gas flows?

options.A: Pressure gauge
options.B: Pulse oximeter
options.C: Flow meter
options.D: Humidifier bottle

explanation: The flow meter is your best friend for control—it lets you accurately dial in the exact liters per minute prescribed for your patient.

question: When do you typically hook up a humidification bottle filled with sterile water to an oxygen setup?

options.A: Only when the patient is diagnosed with an active lung infection
options.B: Whenever oxygen is delivered at any flow rate below one liter
options.C: When delivering higher flow rates that can dry the nasal passages
options.D: To cool the temperature of the gas before it enters the nose

explanation: Medical oxygen is very dry and can irritate the nose at higher flows. Adding sterile water for humidification keeps your patient nice and comfortable!

question: What is the best bed position for a patient struggling to breathe who needs supplemental oxygen?

options.A: Prone position facing down on the bed
options.B: Semi-Fowler's or high-Fowler's position
options.C: Flat on the back with legs slightly raised
options.D: Trendelenburg position with tilted head

explanation: Sitting upright in Semi- or High-Fowler's position lets gravity help expand the lungs fully, making every breath much easier for your patient.

question: You notice raw, red skin inside a patient's nostrils while getting ready to put on a nasal cannula. What should you do first?

options.A: Scrub the irritated skin vigorously with an antiseptic alcohol wipe
options.B: Switch the patient immediately to an invasive mechanical ventilator
options.C: Refuse to start the oxygen therapy until the skin is completely healed
options.D: Document the finding, apply a water-based lubricant if ordered, and monitor the area closely

explanation: Always check and document skin status! Protecting sore areas with safe, water-based lubricants helps prevent further friction without stopping vital oxygen.

question: How should the little prongs of a nasal cannula face when you put them into a patient's nose?

options.A: Flattened sideways
options.B: Pointing straight up
options.C: Curving downward
options.D: Tilted backward

explanation: They are shaped to match human anatomy! Pointing them downward ensures they slide comfortably along the natural curve of the nasal passages.

question: Why is it smart to check that gas is actually flowing out of the cannula prongs before placing them on the patient?

options.A: To measure the exact oxygen percentage in the room air
options.B: To confirm the equipment works and gas is actively delivering
options.C: To clear out any trapped dust from the manufacturing factory
options.D: To warm up the cold gas before it touches the sensitive nasal lining

explanation: A quick check saves a lot of trouble—you want to make sure there isn't a kinked tube or a closed valve blocking air before it reaches your patient.

question: What is the usual maximum flow rate recommended for a standard nasal cannula?

options.A: 2 Liters per minute
options.B: 12 Liters per minute
options.C: 20 Liters per minute
options.D: 6 Liters per minute

explanation: We usually stick to 1 to 6 Liters per minute for standard cannulas. Going higher mostly just dries out the nose without giving extra benefits.

question: Why does the actual amount of oxygen (FiO2) a patient receives from a nasal cannula vary from person to person?

options.A: Different hospitals calibrate their wall oxygen outlets to different pressures
options.B: It depends on the patient's breathing rate and depth, which mixes room air with the oxygen
options.C: Patients absorb oxygen at different speeds through their skin
options.D: The plastic tubing stretches or shrinks based on the room temperature

explanation: Because a nasal cannula is an open system, patients breathe in regular room air right along with the oxygen. How fast or deep they breathe changes the exact mix!

question: What is an important daily nursing task for a patient on continuous nasal cannula oxygen?

options.A: Inspecting skin behind the ears and providing nasal hygiene
options.B: Keeping the patient strictly confined to bedrest
options.C: Changing the wall flow meter every four hours
options.D: Washing the entire length of the plastic tubing with soap

explanation: Plastic tubing can rub against delicate skin behind the ears and in the nose. Regular checks and basic hygiene keep your patient safe and comfortable.

question: Your patient on a nasal cannula complains of a dry, sore throat and a mild nosebleed. What is your best nursing action?

options.A: Increase the oxygen flow rate to flush the nasal passages
options.B: Recommend adding humidification to the oxygen setup as prescribed
options.C: Remove the oxygen permanently and document refusal of care
options.D: Switch the patient to a tight-fitting non-rebreather mask

explanation: Dry medical gas can be tough on delicate mucous membranes. Adding moisture (humidification) is the perfect fix to soothe that dryness and irritation.

question: Which of these substances should you NEVER use to soothe dry nostrils during oxygen therapy because of fire risks?

options.A: Petroleum jelly
options.B: Aqueous cream
options.C: Water-based gel
options.D: Saline nasal spray

explanation: Never use petroleum-based products around oxygen! They are flammable and can easily catch fire in an oxygen-rich environment—always stick to water-based options.

question: Why do oxygen cylinders and wall outlets always need strict 'No Smoking' safety signs nearby?

options.A: Oxygen strongly supports combustion and makes fires spread rapidly
options.B: Tobacco smoke clogs the small holes in the nasal cannula prongs
options.C: Smoking interferes with the machine's internal electrical circuits
options.D: The smell of smoke ruins the purity of the medical gas supply

explanation: Oxygen itself doesn't burn, but it feeds fires aggressively. Even a tiny spark can turn into a massive flame in seconds around supplemental oxygen!

question: What primary method do electronic blood pressure devices use to measure arterial pressure?

options.A: Palpation of radial pulses
options.B: Auscultation of Korotkoff sounds
options.C: Oscillometric measurement
options.D: Direct intra-arterial catheterization

explanation: Electronic monitors detect pressure oscillations in the cuff caused by blood flow rather than listening for physical sounds through a stethoscope. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T1#GNS212_U4_T1_h1)

question: Which specific pressure point do electronic algorithms calculate directly from the maximum oscillation amplitude?

options.A: Diastolic blood pressure
options.B: Mean arterial pressure
options.C: Pulse pressure
options.D: Systolic blood pressure

explanation: The point of maximum oscillation corresponds to the mean arterial pressure, from which systolic and diastolic values are mathematically derived. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T1#GNS212_U4_T1_h1)

question: What is a major advantage of electronic blood pressure monitors over manual auscultation?

options.A: Absolute immunity to motion artifact and patient movement
options.B: Flawless accuracy during severe cardiac arrhythmias
options.C: Elimination of operator dependency on hearing Korotkoff sounds
options.D: Inability to ever require maintenance or recalibration

explanation: Automated devices remove the need for the user to interpret sounds via a stethoscope, reducing human error related to hearing acuity. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T1#GNS212_U4_T1_h2)

question: Why might an electronic blood pressure monitor fail to provide a reading in a patient with severe atrial fibrillation?

options.A: The irregular pulse amplitude confuses the algorithmic pulse wave detection
options.B: The device automatically locks when it detects a fast heart rate
options.C: The stethoscope connection port becomes blocked by electrical signals
options.D: Atrial fibrillation causes the cuff material to degrade rapidly

explanation: Oscillometric algorithms rely on steady, predictable pulse amplitude changes during deflation, which irregular rhythms disrupt. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T1#GNS212_U4_T1_h2)

question: What effect does using a blood pressure cuff that is too small have on the resulting reading?

options.A: It falsely elevates the blood pressure reading
options.B: It keeps the blood pressure reading completely normal
options.C: It prevents the electronic device from turning on
options.D: It falsely lowers the blood pressure reading

explanation: A narrow cuff requires higher pressure to occlude the brachial artery, resulting in falsely high systolic and diastolic numbers. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T1#GNS212_U4_T1_h3)

question: A patient arrives at the clinic running late and immediately sits down for a blood pressure check. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Use a manual cuff immediately because electronic devices require no rest period
options.B: Take the blood pressure on the lower leg instead to avoid resting time
options.C: Proceed immediately with the measurement since time is limited in the clinic
options.D: Allow the patient to rest quietly for five minutes before taking the measurement

explanation: Physical activity and rushing elevate blood pressure; resting for five minutes ensures a baseline reading rather than an artifactual elevation. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T1#GNS212_U4_T1_h3)

question: Why does a patient talking or moving during an automated blood pressure measurement cause an inaccurate reading?

options.A: Speech patterns generate sound waves that interfere with the digital screen
options.B: Movement causes the internal battery to lose electrical charge rapidly
options.C: Talking increases the patient's height instantly and alters hydrostatic pressure
options.D: Muscle movement creates physical artifacts that distort the oscillation signals

explanation: Body movement creates random pressure changes in the cuff that the microprocessor mistakes for arterial pulsations. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T1#GNS212_U4_T1_h4)

question: Which of the following conditions is NOT typically a primary cause of interference with electronic blood pressure readings?

options.A: Severe muscle tremors or shivering
options.B: Advanced peripheral vascular disease
options.C: Incorrect cuff sizing for the limb
options.D: Relaxed posture in a quiet room

explanation: A relaxed posture in a quiet environment is the ideal condition for obtaining an accurate measurement, not a source of interference. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T1#GNS212_U4_T1_h4)

question: How often should electronic blood pressure monitors typically undergo professional biomedical calibration?

options.A: Only when the outer casing looks dirty
options.B: Annually or after physical impact
options.C: After every single patient measurement
options.D: Every ten years regardless of usage

explanation: Routine annual checks and recalibrations after drops ensure the internal pressure sensors remain accurate over time. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T1#GNS212_U4_T1_h5)

question: An electronic blood pressure machine repeatedly stops inflating halfway and displays an error code. What is the most logical initial troubleshooting step?

options.A: Check for air leaks in the tubing and verify secure connections
options.B: Discard the entire device and purchase a brand new model
options.C: Immerse the electronic monitor in water to clean internal valves
options.D: Increase the blood pressure cuff inflation pressure manually with a bulb

explanation: Incomplete inflation and error codes are frequently caused by loose tubing connections or air leaks preventing pressure build-up. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T1#GNS212_U4_T1_h5)

question: What is the appropriate nursing action when an electronic blood pressure monitor yields an unexpectedly critical or abnormal reading?

options.A: Wait twenty-four hours before checking the patient again
options.B: Ignore the reading entirely and document normal blood pressure
options.C: Assume the machine is always correct and immediately administer drugs
options.D: Verify the finding by performing a manual auscultated measurement

explanation: Unexpectedly abnormal automated readings should be cross-checked manually to rule out device malfunction or artifact before clinical intervention. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T1#GNS212_U4_T1_h6)

question: What key detail must be included when documenting a blood pressure measurement in the clinical record?

options.A: The specific limb and patient position used
options.B: The brand name of the electronic battery used
options.C: The room temperature at the time of the check
options.D: The serial number of the stethoscope

explanation: Documenting the anatomical site, position, and method ensures future measurements are taken under consistent, comparable conditions. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T1#GNS212_U4_T1_h6)

question: What is the primary advantage of portable monitors over traditional wall-mounted units?

options.A: They eliminate the need for manual charting altogether
options.B: They allow continuous vital sign tracking during patient transport
options.C: They automatically administer emergency medications
options.D: They require no battery power or electrical connection

explanation: Portable monitors are specifically designed to maintain uninterrupted surveillance while moving patients between departments or during transport. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T10#GNS212_U4_T10_h1)

question: How do portable monitors particularly benefit nursing workflows in high-workload environments?

options.A: By reducing the frequency of required physician rounds
options.B: By completely preventing equipment calibration errors
options.C: By providing early warning signs of clinical deterioration during transport
options.D: By replacing the need for physical assessments by qualified nurses

explanation: Continuous tracking outside the static ICU setting ensures that sudden changes in patient status are caught immediately. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T10#GNS212_U4_T10_h1)

question: Which portable monitoring device is best suited for continuously tracking a patient's electrical heart rhythm while they walk around the ward?

options.A: Handheld pulse oximeters
options.B: Multiparameter transport monitors
options.C: Telemetry transmitters
options.D: Bedside mechanical ventilators

explanation: Telemetry units are worn by ambulatory patients to continuously transmit cardiac rhythm data wirelessly to a central monitoring station. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T10#GNS212_U4_T10_h2)

question: A nurse needs to perform a quick spot-check of oxygen saturation on multiple patients in a busy general ward. Which device is most appropriate?

options.A: Handheld pulse oximeter
options.B: Multiparameter transport monitor
options.C: Wireless telemetry transmitter
options.D: Portable capnograph

explanation: Handheld pulse oximeters are lightweight, portable, and designed specifically for rapid spot-checking of SpO2 and pulse rate. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T10#GNS212_U4_T10_h2)

question: When is the use of a portable continuous monitor clinically justified for a patient?

options.A: When the ward experiences a shortage of traditional wall clocks
options.B: When transporting a critically ill patient requiring vasoactive infusions
options.C: When routine manual vital signs are documented every eight hours
options.D: When the patient is stable and ready for hospital discharge

explanation: Patients on critical infusions or with unstable hemodynamics require uninterrupted monitoring during movement to maintain safety. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T10#GNS212_U4_T10_h3)

question: What is a negative consequence of placing a portable monitor on a stable patient who does not need it?

options.A: Unnecessary alarm fatigue for nursing staff
options.B: Immediate battery failure of the device
options.C: Automatic deletion of patient records
options.D: Inability to document baseline temperature

explanation: Over-monitoring stable patients generates excessive false or low-priority alarms, desensitizing staff to critical warning signals. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T10#GNS212_U4_T10_h3)

question: What is a common pitfall that causes erroneous non-invasive blood pressure readings on a portable monitor?

options.A: Calibrating the pulse oximeter probe too frequently
options.B: Connecting the device to a wall electrical outlet
options.C: Setting the screen brightness to maximum level
options.D: Using an incorrect cuff size for the patient's limb

explanation: An improperly sized blood pressure cuff directly distorts measurement accuracy, leading to falsely high or low readings. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T10#GNS212_U4_T10_h4)

question: A nurse is preparing to transfer an unstable patient to radiology with a portable monitor. What is the most critical pre-transport check?

options.A: Replacing all disposable electrodes with gold-plated sensors
options.B: Ensuring the internal monitor battery is fully charged
options.C: Clearing all historical patient data from the hard drive
options.D: Lowering the alarm volume to avoid disturbing other patients

explanation: During transport, AC power is often unavailable, making a fully charged internal battery essential for continuous monitoring. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T10#GNS212_U4_T10_h4)

question: What should the nurse do first when a portable monitor suddenly displays an alarming drop in oxygen saturation?

options.A: Increase the supplemental oxygen flow rate to maximum
options.B: Immediately silence the alarm and turn off the device
options.C: Assess the patient's clinical status and physical appearance
options.D: Call the biomedical engineering department for a replacement

explanation: Always assess the patient before the equipment to determine if the reading represents a true physiological emergency or a technical artifact. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T10#GNS212_U4_T10_h5)

question: Which type of alarm indicates an immediate threat to patient life on a monitoring system?

options.A: Technical sensor alert
options.B: Advisory notification
options.C: Low-priority prompt
options.D: High-priority alarm

explanation: High-priority alarms denote critical, life-threatening events such as cardiac arrest or severe hypoxia requiring immediate intervention. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T10#GNS212_U4_T10_h5)

question: What is the primary infection control practice required for portable monitors between patient uses?

options.A: Exposing the device to direct sunlight for two hours
options.B: Replacing all internal circuit boards after every single transport
options.C: Submerging the entire electronic monitor in chemical sterilizing solution
options.D: Wiping down all surfaces and reusable sensors with approved hospital disinfectants

explanation: Surface disinfection with appropriate hospital-grade wipes prevents cross-contamination between patients who share portable equipment. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T10#GNS212_U4_T10_h6)

question: What is NOT a recommended step when initially troubleshooting a portable monitor displaying an error signal?

options.A: Checking that all external cables are securely plugged in
options.B: Immediately discarding the monitor into general waste
options.C: Inspecting sensors for proper placement and contact
options.D: Verifying the power source and battery charge level

explanation: Equipment should be systematically checked and evaluated by biomedical services rather than discarded prematurely upon encountering an error. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T10#GNS212_U4_T10_h6)

question: What is the primary shift in healthcare delivery enabled by wearable devices?

options.A: Reducing the cost of pharmaceutical manufacturing significantly
options.B: Replacing all bedside nursing documentation with automated logs
options.C: Moving from episodic clinic visits to continuous health intelligence
options.D: Eliminating the need for physical diagnostic laboratories entirely

explanation: Wearables allow ongoing physiological data collection outside traditional appointments, changing care from periodic checks to continuous monitoring. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T11#GNS212_U4_T11_h1)

question: Why has the perception of consumer wearable technology changed among clinical professionals?

options.A: Devices have advanced from simple fitness trackers to multi-sensor clinical tools
options.B: Patients refuse to visit clinics without wearing a digital wristband
options.C: Governments now mandate that every citizen wear a certified health monitor
options.D: Hospitals no longer use traditional diagnostic machines like ECGs

explanation: Modern wearables measure advanced parameters like ECG and oxygen saturation, bridging the gap between consumer gadgets and clinical equipment. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T11#GNS212_U4_T11_h1)

question: Where is the sensing filament of a continuous glucose monitor typically placed?

options.A: Intramuscular muscle
options.B: Intravenous vessel
options.C: Subcutaneous tissue
options.D: Superficial epidermis

explanation: CGMs use a small sensor inserted just beneath the skin to measure glucose concentrations in the interstitial fluid. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T11#GNS212_U4_T11_h2)

question: What distinguishes smart textiles from traditional wrist-worn fitness bands?

options.A: Smart textiles only function when submerged in sterile liquid solutions
options.B: Smart textiles are strictly regulated as surgical implants
options.C: Smart textiles weave conductive sensors directly into clothing fabric
options.D: Smart textiles do not require any form of battery power to operate

explanation: These garments integrate monitoring capabilities into everyday clothing to capture data like respiration and posture seamlessly. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T11#GNS212_U4_T11_h2)

question: Which technology do optical wearable sensors use to estimate heart rate and blood oxygen?

options.A: Photoplethysmography
options.B: Ultrasound doppler
options.C: Spirometry analysis
options.D: Electroencephalography

explanation: Optical sensors shine light through the skin and measure changes in light absorption caused by pulsating blood volume, known as photoplethysmography. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T11#GNS212_U4_T11_h3)

question: How do accelerometer sensors contribute to patient health assessments?

options.A: By analyzing chemical markers present in the patient's sweat
options.B: By measuring physical movement, gait patterns, and activity levels
options.C: By recording electrical impulses generated by cardiac muscle fibers
options.D: By detecting micro-fluctuations in blood glucose concentrations

explanation: Accelerometers track motion and spatial orientation, helping nurses evaluate a patient's physical activity, mobility, and fall risks. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T11#GNS212_U4_T11_h3)

question: What is the primary advantage of ambulatory wearable monitoring over a standard clinic checkup?

options.A: Reducing hospital admission rates to exactly zero percent
options.B: Eliminating the need for professional nursing clinical judgment
options.C: Capturing transient, intermittent events during daily life activities
options.D: Guaranteeing zero false-positive readings during diagnostic screening

explanation: Many conditions occur unpredictably; continuous ambulatory monitoring catches these episodic events outside the clinical environment. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T11#GNS212_U4_T11_h4)

question: A patient experiences infrequent heart palpitations that never appear during routine ECGs. What is the clinical benefit of using a wearable heart monitor in this scenario?

options.A: It automatically cures the underlying arrhythmia using low-frequency electrical impulses
options.B: It records continuous data over weeks, capturing the palpitations when they happen
options.C: It permanently stops the patient from feeling any further physical discomfort
options.D: It transmits an electric shock to reset the heart rhythm safely at home

explanation: Longitudinal monitoring increases the likelihood of capturing irregular rhythms that escape detection during brief snapshot assessments. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T11#GNS212_U4_T11_h4)

question: What is an important responsibility of the nurse when managing data from patient wearables?

options.A: Writing proprietary software code to update the wearable's internal operating system
options.B: Manually calibrating every microchip component within the sensor hardware
options.C: Replacing the physical battery packs inside sealed consumer wristbands
options.D: Triaging data streams to separate genuine physiological alerts from movement artifacts

explanation: Nurses must review incoming data critically, filtering out false alarms caused by motion or poor skin contact before notifying physicians. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T11#GNS212_U4_T11_h5)

question: Why is patient education regarding skin hygiene important for individuals using adhesive patch wearables?

options.A: To ensure the device transmits data at a faster wireless frequency
options.B: To prevent moisture accumulation and localized skin irritation or breakdown
options.C: To prevent the sensor from picking up ambient room temperature
options.D: To keep the internal battery fully charged throughout the week

explanation: Prolonged contact with adhesive patches and trapped sweat can lead to contact dermatitis or skin breakdown if hygiene is neglected. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T11#GNS212_U4_T11_h5)

question: How do continuous glucose monitors improve the daily management routine for diabetic patients?

options.A: By restricting the patient's daily carbohydrate intake automatically
options.B: By automatically injecting precise doses of intravenous insulin
options.C: By eliminating the need for frequent painful finger-prick blood tests
options.D: By curing the underlying pancreatic beta-cell autoimmune destruction

explanation: CGMs provide ongoing interstitial glucose readings, sparing patients from frequent manual lancet pricks while offering real-time trend arrows. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T11#GNS212_U4_T11_h6)

question: What is the psychological and behavioral benefit of real-time physiological feedback from wearables in chronic illness?

options.A: It removes all personal responsibility for health management from the patient
options.B: It fosters self-efficacy by showing patients how lifestyle choices directly affect their health
options.C: It induces chronic anxiety that forces patients to rest constantly
options.D: It completely replaces the need for professional clinical consultations

explanation: Seeing direct correlations between daily habits and physiological data motivates patients to adhere to treatment plans and adopt healthier lifestyles. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T11#GNS212_U4_T11_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a major ethical concern associated with consumer health wearables?

options.A: Risk of health insurance discrimination based on activity tracking
options.B: Potential unauthorized access to sensitive biological data by third parties
options.C: Widening healthcare disparities due to unequal device affordability
options.D: Guaranteed elimination of all chronic illnesses in the population

explanation: Wearables help monitor and manage conditions, but they do not guarantee the elimination of chronic illness. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T11#GNS212_U4_T11_h7)

question: Why are commercial cloud servers used by some consumer wearables considered a security vulnerability?

options.A: They prevent nurses from accessing local hospital intranet systems
options.B: They may lack the stringent privacy protections required for traditional medical health records
options.C: They operate without any electricity or backup power generation
options.D: They automatically delete all patient physiological data every twenty-four hours

explanation: Consumer-grade apps and cloud storage often fall outside strict medical privacy regulations, leaving personal health data vulnerable to breaches. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T11#GNS212_U4_T11_h7)

question: What is a primary infrastructural barrier to using rechargeable medical wearables in many Nigerian rural primary health centers?

options.A: Unreliable electrical power grids and frequent blackouts
options.B: Strict government bans on wireless radio frequency devices
options.C: A complete absence of mobile cellular telephone towers
options.D: Excessive humidity freezing the electronic components instantly

explanation: Consistent electricity is essential for charging monitoring hardware and maintaining server connections, making power instability a major hurdle. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T11#GNS212_U4_T11_h8)

question: How do economic factors primarily influence the adoption of wearable health devices in low-resource settings?

options.A: Patients prefer expensive imported devices over locally manufactured alternatives
options.B: High out-of-pocket costs make advanced monitoring tools unaffordable for the average citizen
options.C: Free government distribution leads to massive device hoarding in urban warehouses
options.D: Commercial manufacturers provide unlimited free replacements for lost equipment

explanation: Because health financing relies heavily on out-of-pocket spending, expensive wearable technology remains out of reach for vulnerable populations. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T11#GNS212_U4_T11_h8)

question: What is the primary characteristic of tele-nursing?

options.A: The administration of intravenous medication without direct physical supervision
options.B: The exclusive use of paper records for long-distance patient communication
options.C: The complete replacement of bedside hospital nursing by artificial intelligence
options.D: The delivery of nursing care using information and communication technologies

explanation: Tele-nursing relies on digital tools and communication channels to provide care remotely rather than requiring a traditional face-to-face encounter. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T12#GNS212_U4_T12_h1)

question: How does remote patient monitoring differ from standard telephone triage?

options.A: Remote patient monitoring tracks continuous physiological data via connected devices
options.B: Telephone triage requires specialized surgical equipment installed in the patient's home
options.C: Remote patient monitoring is only performed by physicians in tertiary facilities
options.D: Telephone triage replaces the need for any subsequent physical health assessments

explanation: While telephone triage often involves verbal reporting of symptoms, remote patient monitoring uses objective, device-driven data feeds such as blood glucose or vital signs. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T12#GNS212_U4_T12_h1)

question: What was a primary driver for early remote healthcare communication before the internet era?

options.A: Completely eliminating the need for any local community clinics
options.B: Replacing physical nursing textbooks with digital PDF files
options.C: Reducing hospital operational costs by closing urban emergency rooms
options.D: Providing medical guidance to geographically isolated individuals

explanation: Early tele-health and tele-nursing initiatives emerged primarily to bridge the distance gap for rural outposts, ships at sea, and isolated populations. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T12#GNS212_U4_T12_h2)

question: What factor has most significantly accelerated the recent growth of tele-nursing worldwide?

options.A: The total replacement of professional nurses by automated software
options.B: Mandatory global legislation prohibiting in-person clinical consultations
options.C: The complete disappearance of chronic illness in urban populations
options.D: Widespread availability of smartphones and expanding internet access

explanation: Consumer-grade technology and mobile data networks have made video consultations and remote monitoring accessible to a much broader demographic. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T12#GNS212_U4_T12_h2)

question: Why is data encryption critical in tele-nursing software applications?

options.A: To protect patient confidentiality and prevent unauthorized access to health records
options.B: To increase the speed at which video streams load on mobile devices
options.C: To automatically diagnose complex cardiac arrhythmias without nurse intervention
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing mobile data bundles

explanation: Encryption ensures that sensitive health information transmitted across digital networks cannot be intercepted or read by unauthorized parties. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T12#GNS212_U4_T12_h3)

question: A nurse practicing in an area with frequent power outages and expensive internet should prioritize which technological feature?

options.A: High-definition virtual reality headsets for immersive patient assessments
options.B: Constant real-time streaming of high-resolution surgical video feeds
options.C: Low-bandwidth compatibility and offline data synchronization capabilities
options.D: Automated robotic arms that perform physical injections in the home

question: What is a primary goal of utilizing tele-nursing for chronic disease management?

options.A: Permanent elimination of all prescription medications for the patient
options.B: Mandating daily hospital visits for routine vital sign checks
options.C: Replacing primary care physicians with automated diagnostic machines
options.D: Regular tracking of biometric data to detect early signs of clinical deterioration

explanation: Continuous or regular monitoring allows nurses to intervene early when a chronic condition begins to destabilize, preventing acute crises. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T12#GNS212_U4_T12_h4)

question: A patient discharged three days ago following a major abdominal surgery calls the tele-nursing line reporting mild, localized redness around the incision. What is the most appropriate initial nursing action?

options.A: Assess the characteristics of the redness, drainage, and systemic symptoms via targeted questioning
options.B: Schedule an emergency surgical revision in the operating theatre for later that evening
options.C: Advise the patient to immediately stop all prescribed antibiotics without consulting the physician
options.D: Tell the patient that minor skin changes after surgery are completely normal and require no attention

explanation: The nurse must first gather focused clinical data through systematic questioning to determine if the wound is healing normally or showing signs of infection. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T12#GNS212_U4_T12_h4)

question: Which regulatory body is primarily responsible for setting professional practice standards for nurses in Nigeria?

options.A: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.B: Nigerian Communications Commission
options.C: Standard Organisation of Nigeria
options.D: Federal Ministry of Information and Culture

explanation: The NMCN is the statutory body charged with the regulation, control, and standardization of nursing education and practice in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T12#GNS212_U4_T12_h5)

question: Why is cross-border tele-nursing legally and ethically challenging for a practicing nurse?

options.A: Technology platforms automatically block voice communication between different time zones
options.B: Digital data packets are unable to cross international borders due to physical weight
options.C: Licensure requirements and scope of practice rules vary across different states or countries
options.D: Patients located in other regions are legally prohibited from speaking with foreign nurses

explanation: Nurses must be legally authorized to practice in the jurisdiction where the patient is physically located at the time of the encounter. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T12#GNS212_U4_T12_h5)

question: What is a major advantage of tele-nursing for patients living in remote rural communities?

options.A: Complete replacement of self-care with automated nursing systems
options.B: Free provision of high-end computer hardware and unlimited electricity
options.C: Reduction of travel barriers and improved access to health guidance
options.D: Guaranteed elimination of all chronic health conditions

explanation: Remote care overcomes geographical distance, allowing patients far from urban centers to consult healthcare professionals without arduous travel. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T12#GNS212_U4_T12_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a recognized challenge in tele-nursing practice?

options.A: The total elimination of human clinical errors in treatment plans
options.B: The limitation of physical assessments without hands-on palpation
options.C: The potential for technical failures like internet drops during calls
options.D: The presence of a digital divide affecting elderly or low-income populations

explanation: Tele-nursing does not eliminate human error; in fact, interpreting clinical signs remotely can introduce unique assessment challenges. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T12#GNS212_U4_T12_h6)

question: How are wearable biosensors expected to influence the future of tele-nursing?

options.A: By eliminating the need for any software security protocols
options.B: By providing continuous, real-time physiological data streams for nurse monitoring
options.C: By serving as permanent surgical replacements for malfunctioning organs
options.D: By completely replacing the need for human critical thinking in nursing

explanation: Wearable sensors feed continuous health metrics into remote monitoring systems, allowing nurses to track trends and detect early warning signs. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T12#GNS212_U4_T12_h7)

question: What educational shift is necessary to prepare nursing students for the future of healthcare delivery?

options.A: Integrating digital health competencies and informatics into foundational curricula
options.B: Requiring all students to obtain a degree in computer engineering
options.C: Removing clinical patient interaction entirely in favor of computer simulations
options.D: Focusing exclusively on manual paper charting and analog telephone skills

explanation: To thrive in tech-enabled environments, nursing students must become proficient in health informatics and digital communication tools alongside clinical skills. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T12#GNS212_U4_T12_h7)

question: What is the primary electrical rhythm treated by an automated external defibrillator?

options.A: Asystole
options.B: Ventricular fibrillation
options.C: Sinus bradycardia
options.D: Atrial flutter

explanation: Ventricular fibrillation is a chaotic, shockable cardiac rhythm where the ventricles quiver instead of pumping blood, which the device is specifically engineered to detect and treat. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T13#GNS212_U4_T13_h1)

question: Why are automated external defibrillators designed for use by bystanders with minimal medical training?

options.A: They bypass the need for cardiopulmonary resuscitation entirely during an emergency.
options.B: They automatically administer emergency medications through transdermal patches.
options.C: They allow the user to manually adjust the voltage output based on patient weight.
options.D: They incorporate automated rhythm analysis and voice prompts to guide the operator.

explanation: Simplified interfaces with clear voice instructions allow individuals without clinical training to safely operate the unit during high-stress cardiac emergencies. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T13#GNS212_U4_T13_h1)

question: What action should be taken if a patient is lying in a pool of water when a shock is advised?

options.A: Apply rubber insulating gloves and proceed with the shock immediately.
options.B: Move the patient to a dry surface before applying the electrode pads.
options.C: Increase the distance between the electrode pads to compensate for moisture.
options.D: Skip the device entirely and rely solely on manual chest compressions.

explanation: Water conducts electricity poorly for the heart and creates dangerous stray current pathways that can injure rescuers, necessitating a dry environment. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T13#GNS212_U4_T13_h2)

question: Which of the following scenarios represents a correct application for an automated external defibrillator?

options.A: An adult collapse victim who is unresponsive and gasping irregularly
options.B: An elderly person found in asystole with no electrical cardiac activity
options.C: A child with a slow, regular pulse and adequate spontaneous breathing
options.D: A conscious patient experiencing acute chest pain and diaphoresis

explanation: Unresponsiveness and agonal or absent breathing are classic signs of sudden cardiac arrest requiring immediate deployment of emergency equipment. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T13#GNS212_U4_T13_h2)

question: What is the function of the indicator light on a stored automated external defibrillator?

options.A: To show that daily self-tests and battery status are functioning properly
options.B: To indicate the exact percentage of remaining electrical energy
options.C: To signal when the high-voltage capacitor is fully charged for a shock
options.D: To illuminate the patient's chest during dark emergency scenarios

explanation: Routine self-tests run automatically by the machine report their operational status through a simple indicator light or status window. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T13#GNS212_U4_T13_h3)

question: Why are adhesive electrode pads coated with a specialized conductive gel?

options.A: To deliver local anesthetic agents that minimize patient discomfort
options.B: To cool the skin tissue and prevent superficial thermal burns from the current
options.C: To permanently anchor the pads to the skin so they never shift during transport
options.D: To ensure optimal electrical contact and reduce skin resistance during shock delivery

explanation: Conductive gel bridges microscopic gaps between the metal pad and the skin, lowering impedance so the electrical current passes effectively into the myocardium. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T13#GNS212_U4_T13_h3)

question: Where should the two adhesive electrode pads be placed on an adult patient's chest?

options.A: Upper left chest and lower right abdomen near the umbilicus
options.B: Center of the sternum and directly over the apex of the heart
options.C: Both shoulders symmetrically on the anterior pectoral muscles
options.D: Upper right chest below the collarbone and lower left lateral chest

explanation: This standard anterolateral placement ensures the electrical current vector passes directly through the mass of the heart ventricles. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T13#GNS212_U4_T13_h4)

question: What critical action must a rescuer perform immediately before pressing the shock button?

options.A: Manually adjust the energy dose based on the patient's age.
options.B: Verify that the patient's pulse has returned to a normal sinus rate.
options.C: Inject emergency adrenaline through the intravenous line.
options.D: Ensure that no person is touching or in contact with the patient.

explanation: Touching the patient during shock delivery can cause the electrical current to pass through the rescuer, resulting in injury or accidental shock. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T13#GNS212_U4_T13_h4)

question: How does integrating an automated external defibrillator with chest compressions impact patient survival?

options.A: It eliminates the metabolic demand for oxygen in ischemic myocardial tissue.
options.B: It automatically regulates the depth of manual chest compressions via audio feedback.
options.C: It minimizes hands-off intervals, maintaining vital coronary and cerebral perfusion.
options.D: It replaces the need for chest compressions entirely once the pads are attached.

explanation: Continuous high-quality compressions combined with prompt rhythm analysis preserve blood flow to the brain and heart until a normal rhythm returns. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T13#GNS212_U4_T13_h5)

question: When should chest compressions be resumed after the unit delivers a shock?

options.A: Immediately without waiting for a rhythm check
options.B: When the patient begins spontaneous breathing movements
options.C: Only after checking for a palpable carotid pulse for ten seconds
options.D: After the machine completes two additional cycles of voice analysis

explanation: Current resuscitation guidelines dictate starting chest compressions immediately after a shock, waiting for two minutes before the next automated rhythm analysis. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T13#GNS212_U4_T13_h5)

question: What is the correct procedure if a transdermal medication patch covers the exact spot where an electrode pad needs to go?

options.A: Select an alternative brand of device that transmits through medication.
options.B: Cut a hole in the center of the adhesive pad to accommodate the patch.
options.C: Place the electrode pad directly on top of the patch to protect the skin.
options.D: Remove the patch, wipe the skin clean, and then apply the pad.

explanation: Transdermal patches can block electrical current or cause chemical burns, so they must be removed and the skin cleaned prior to pad placement. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T13#GNS212_U4_T13_h6)

question: Why are pediatric attenuation systems used when defibrillating small children?

options.A: To increase the speed of rhythm analysis for rapid heart rates in infants
options.B: To decrease the electrical energy output to a safe level for smaller body masses
options.C: To allow the use of standard adult pads without modifying their placement
options.D: To convert the device into a manual defibrillator for precise dosage control

explanation: Children require substantially lower joules than adults to avoid myocardial damage from excessive electrical energy during defibrillation. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T13#GNS212_U4_T13_h6)

question: What primary items on an automated external defibrillator have expiration dates that must be routinely inspected?

options.A: Adhesive electrode pads and backup batteries
options.B: The emergency speaker system and voice prompt module
options.C: The high-voltage capacitor and internal motherboard
options.D: The external hard casing and carrying handle

explanation: Adhesive gel dries out over time and battery chemistry degrades, making regular inspection of pads and batteries vital for operational readiness. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T13#GNS212_U4_T13_h7)

question: What action is required if a unit fails its automated daily self-test and emits a continuous warning chirp?

options.A: Reset the internal clock to silence the alarm until the next code blue.
options.B: Move the unit to a cooler storage room to stabilize internal circuitry.
options.C: Use the manual override switch to bypass the self-test diagnostics.
options.D: Remove the unit from service immediately and replace faulty components.

explanation: A failed self-test indicates potential operational failure during a crisis, requiring immediate removal for maintenance or component replacement. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T13#GNS212_U4_T13_h7)

question: Which detail is essential to include in the nursing documentation following a cardiac arrest resuscitation event?

options.A: The serial number and manufacturing date of the electrode pads
options.B: The personal contact information of all bystander rescuers present
options.C: The brand name of the cardiopulmonary resuscitation backboard used
options.D: The total number of shocks delivered and the patient's response

explanation: Accurate clinical records must capture key resuscitation milestones, including shock counts and subsequent rhythm changes, for continuity of care. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T13#GNS212_U4_T13_h8)

question: What is the clinical value of retrieving the digital data stored on the unit's internal memory card after a code?

options.A: It allows the hospital to bill insurance companies for the precise electrical energy consumed.
options.B: It prevents the device from requiring maintenance checks for the next six months.
options.C: It provides an accurate electronic record of cardiac rhythms and device interventions for medical review.
options.D: It automatically updates the patient's electronic health record with their medication allergies.

explanation: Downloaded device data yields precise ECG tracings and timing logs that help clinicians analyze resuscitation performance and post-arrest care. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T13#GNS212_U4_T13_h8)

question: What is the primary operational advantage of infrared thermometers in clinical settings?

options.A: Permanent storage of patient biometric histories
options.B: Direct measurement of blood pressure simultaneously
options.C: Rapid and non-invasive temperature assessment
options.D: Absolute elimination of cleaning protocols

explanation: Infrared thermometers are valued in clinical practice primarily because they provide quick readings without requiring invasive contact or lengthy insertion times. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h1)

question: Why are glass mercury thermometers being phased out in favor of infrared alternatives in busy wards?

options.A: Infrared sensors directly measure internal core blood chemistry
options.B: Glass thermometers carry risks of breakage and toxic exposure
options.C: Mercury devices only function in sub-zero climates
options.D: Infrared models are completely immune to environmental temperature shifts

explanation: The fragile nature of glass and the toxicity of liquid mercury present safety hazards in busy environments, making non-glass alternatives safer for patients and staff. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h1)

question: What component inside an infrared thermometer converts absorbed thermal radiation into an electrical signal?

options.A: A piezoelectric crystal
options.B: A standard glass bulb
options.C: A mercury reservoir
options.D: A thermopile detector

explanation: The thermopile acts as the core sensor, absorbing focused infrared energy and converting it into a measurable electrical voltage. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h2)

question: What is the function of the internal microprocessor in an infrared thermometer?

options.A: Heats the probe tip to match core body temperature
options.B: Compensates for surrounding ambient temperature variations
options.C: Sterilizes the sensor surface automatically after use
options.D: Generates the infrared beam that scans the skin

explanation: Ambient temperature can distort raw sensor data, so the microprocessor applies algorithmic corrections to ensure the displayed value reflects the true body temperature. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h2)

question: Why is the tympanic membrane considered an ideal site for estimating core body temperature?

options.A: It registers lower readings than any other body cavity
options.B: It shares a direct blood supply with the hypothalamus
options.C: It is completely immune to accumulation of cerumen
options.D: It sits outside the skull away from major blood vessels

explanation: The eardrum and the brain's thermal control center share arterial blood flow, making tympanic readings closely aligned with true core temperature. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h3)

question: A temporal artery thermometer determines core temperature by scanning which anatomical structure?

options.A: The anterior fontanelle found in newborn infant skulls
options.B: The mastoid bone situated directly behind the ear lobe
options.C: The superficial vessel running across the forehead and temple
options.D: The carotid pulse point located deep in the anterior neck

explanation: Temporal scanners are specifically engineered to capture peak thermal emission along the path of the superficial temporal artery. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h3)

question: A patient with severe acute otitis media in the left ear should ideally have their temperature measured by which method?

options.A: Using an alternative site or the unaffected right ear
options.B: Inserting the tympanic probe deeply into the infected ear
options.C: Applying a cold compress to the forehead prior to scanning
options.D: Doubling the scan time with a standard tympanic thermometer
